punchline: Kotter says people will give a long change about six to eighteen months to show proof, and then they start leaving.
thirty_sec: In Leading Change, John Kotter makes step six of his model a planned one: short-term wins. People want evidence within about six to eighteen months, he says, or they quit or join the resisters. A win has to be visible, undisputed and tied to the change. So good managers write such goals into the yearly plan, hit them and reward the people involved. And he warns that declaring victory too early is its own mistake.
